newsitem.title: USA: In Home sees $2.1-mln Q3 pretax charge.
newsitem.headline: In Home sees $2.1-mln Q3 pretax charge.

text.p: In Home Health Inc said Wednesday it expects to post a pre-tax restructuring charge in its third quarter of about $2.1 million.
The in-home healthcare company announced plans to restructure its field operations to reduce costs and create a more efficient organization.
The company said it estimates that future cost reductions made possible by the restructuring, on an annualized basis, will increase net income by about $2.5 million.
Key elements of the restructuring include unspecified staff and expense reductions, In Home said.
Six pharmacies will be closed and the company's markets will be serviced by its six remaining pharmacies, it said.
Sites within eight markets will be consolidated, including closing of three sites in multi-site markets and relocation of 10 other sites to more economical facilities, In Home said.
"The company remains committed to growing its extended hours, visit, infusion and hospice product lines," said chief executive Wolfgang von Maack.
"These efficiencies were put in place to improve the operating profit of the company and to better prepare us for the future programs being proposed by Medicare," he said.
With annual revenues of about $125 million, In Home specializes in providing healthcare services to clients of all ages in their own homes.
In Home provides skilled nursing, infusion therapy, hospice, rehabilitation and personal care, through a network of 40 offices in 19 markets located in 14 states.
